items.title: ObservEarth Documentation
items.text: Welcome to the official developer and user documentation for ObservEarth — the next-generation Earth Observation (EO), satellite remote sensing, weather, and environmental analytics platform.

items.title: What is ObservEarth?
items.text:
ObservEarth empowers developers, agritech firms, researchers, forestry managers, urban planners, and environmental analysts to seamlessly access, analyze, and visualize high-resolution multi-spectral and radar satellite imagery alongside hyper-local weather and air quality datasets.

Instead of wrestling with complex raw geospatial data pipelines, gigabyte-sized GeoTIFFs, or complex atmospheric correction algorithms, ObservEarth provides unified RESTful APIs and an intuitive web dashboard.

items.title: 🛰️ Multi-Constellation Satellite Imagery
items.text:
• Sentinel-2 L2A (10m / 20m): Complete European Space Agency (ESA) surface reflectance imagery with automated cloud masking and over 45 vegetation, water, soil, and fire indices.
  • SEN2SR 2.5m Super-Resolution: Deep learning super-resolution pipeline upscaling 10-band Sentinel-2 imagery to ultra-sharp 2.5m resolution for precision agriculture.
  • Sentinel-1 C-Band SAR (10m): Cloud-penetrating all-weather Synthetic Aperture Radar for day and night moisture, flood, and surface structure monitoring across VV and VH polarizations.
  • Landsat 8 & 9 Collection 2 Level 2 (30m): USGS and NASA optical and thermal infrared bands for long-term multi-decadal environmental trend tracking.
  • MODIS Terra & Aqua (250m - 500m): High-temporal frequency daily observations and 16-day composited vegetation products.

items.title: 🌤️ Hyper-Local Weather & Air Quality
items.text:
• Real-time weather observations: Temperature, relative humidity, precipitation, wind speed, wind gusts, solar radiation, and FAO-56 evapotranspiration (ET0).
  • Sub-surface soil telemetry: Soil temperature and volumetric soil moisture across 5 distinct depth layers (surface, 2 cm, 5 cm, 15 cm, 50 cm).
  • Multi-day forecasting & history: 16-day forward weather forecasting and historical meteorological archives.
  • Comprehensive air quality: Complete pollutant metrics including PM2.5, PM10, NO2, SO2, CO, O3, Aerosol Optical Depth (AOD), European AQI, and US EPA AQI.

items.title: ⛰️ Elevation & Terrain Intelligence
items.text:
• Global 30-meter DEM rasters: Topographic elevation models with dynamic elevation statistics (minimum, maximum, mean, and standard deviation).
  • Automated vector contour lines: Contour extraction in GeoJSON and PNG formats with configurable contour intervals (e.g., 5m, 10m, 20m).

items.title: ⚡ Automated Alerts & Notifications
items.text:
• Persistent spatial monitoring: Continuous automated background scanning on your registered Areas of Interest (AOIs).
  • Conditional threshold triggers: Immediate notifications when new satellite scenes detect threshold breaches (e.g., NDVI < 0.35 or NDWI < -0.1).

items.title: Quick Example: First API Call in 30 Seconds
items.text:
All ObservEarth API endpoints require your API key passed in the X-API-Key HTTP header:

# Verify your API key
curl -X POST "https://observearth.com/api/verify-api-key/" \
     -H "X-API-Key: YOUR_API_KEY_HERE" \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json"

Expected response: 

{
  "valid": true
}

items.text: The Air Quality API provides atmospheric chemical concentration metrics, aerosol optical telemetry, and the European Air Quality Index (AQI) centered directly on your registered farm's geographic coordinates.

items.title: Automated Index Alerts & Notifications API
items.text: The Alerts API allows you to configure real-time threshold monitoring on your farms and retrieve triggered alert notifications. Whenever a new satellite scene (Sentinel-2, Sentinel-1, etc.) is ingested, ObservEarth automatically computes your specified index conditions and logs an alert event.

items.title: Endpoint
items.text: GET /api/alerts/

items.title: Operation Summary
items.text: alerts_list

items.title: Why It's Used
items.text: Retrieve all monitoring alert rules configured for your account.

items.title: Headers
items.text: Header Type Description Required X-API-Key String (UUID) Secret API Key Yes

items.title: Responses
items.text:
• 200 OK: Array of active and paused alert rule definitions: 
    [
  {
    "id": "c1d2e3f4-a5b6-7890-1234-56789abcdef0",
    "geometry_id": "123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000",
    "name": "Low NDVI Warning",
    "logic": "AND",
    "is_active": true,
    "monitor_until": "2026-11-30",
    "conditions": [
      {
        "index": "ndvi",
        "operator": "<",
        "threshold": 0.35
      }
    ],
    "created_at": "2026-05-01T10:00:00Z"
  }
]

items.title: cURL Example
items.text:
curl -X GET "https://observearth.com/api/alerts/" \
     -H "X-API-Key: YOUR_API_KEY"

items.text: POST /api/alerts/

items.title: Operation Summary
items.text: alerts_create

items.text: Header Type Description Required X-API-Key String (UUID) Secret API Key Yes Content-Type String application/json Yes

{

  "name": "Vegetation Stress Watch",
  "logic": "AND",
  "monitor_until": "2026-12-31",
  "conditions": [
    {
      "index": "ndvi",
      "operator": "<",
      "threshold": 0.35
    },
    {
      "index": "ndwi",
      "operator": "<",
      "threshold": -0.10
    }
  ]
}
Field Type Description Required Default geometry_id String (UUID) Target farm UUID Yes - name String Descriptive name Yes - logic String AND or OR boolean operator No AND monitor_until String Expiry date (YYYY-MM-DD) Yes - conditions Array List of index condition objects Yes -

items.title: Condition Object Schema
items.text: Property Type Description Valid Values index String Spectral or SAR index ndvi, ndwi, evi, savi, ndre, vv, vh, rvi, etc. operator String Comparison operator <, <=, >, >=, == threshold Number Numerical cutoff Any float

items.title: Responses
items.text:
• 201 Created: Returns created alert object.
  • 400 Bad Request: Validation error (invalid index, operator, or past date).

items.text:
curl -X POST "https://observearth.com/api/alerts/" \
     -H "X-API-Key: YOUR_API_KEY" \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -d '{

       "logic": "AND",

       "conditions": [
         {"index": "ndvi", "operator": "<", "threshold": 0.35}
       ]
     }'

items.title: Digital Elevation Model (DEM) & Contours API
items.text: The DEM & Contours API provides access to the Copernicus 30m Global Digital Elevation Model (COP-DEM-GLO-30) for extracting terrain elevation rasters and parametric topographic contour line vectors.

items.title: Endpoint
items.text: POST /api/dem/

items.title: Operation Summary
items.text: dem_create

items.title: Why It's Used
items.text: Retrieve Digital Elevation Model (DEM) imagery for a geometry from the COP-DEM-GLO-30 collection clipped to parcel boundaries as PNG or 32-bit floating-point GeoTIFF.

items.title: Headers
items.text: Header Type Description Required X-API-Key String (UUID) Secret API Key Yes Content-Type String application/json Yes

items.title: Request Body
items.text:
{
  "geometry_id": "123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000",
  "format": "png",
  "colormap": "greys"
}
Field Type Description Required Default geometry_id String (UUID) UUID of the registered geometry Yes - format String Output format: png or tif No png colormap String Visualization colormap (e.g. greys, terrain, viridis) No greys

items.title: Responses
items.text:
• 200 OK: Elevation imagery raster stream (image/png or image/tiff).
  • 400 Bad Request: Missing geometry_id or invalid format.
  • 401 Unauthorized: Authentication missing or invalid.
  • 404 Not Found: Geometry does not exist.

items.title: cURL Example
items.text:
curl -X POST "https://observearth.com/api/dem/" \
     -H "X-API-Key: YOUR_API_KEY" \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -d '{
       "geometry_id": "YOUR_GEOMETRY_ID",
       "format": "png",
       "colormap": "terrain"
     }' --output elevation_dem.png

items.title: API Overview & Standards
items.text: The ObservEarth REST API provides unified access to multi-constellation satellite imagery, meteorological telemetry, terrain elevation models, and environmental analytics.

items.title: Base URL
items.text:
All API requests are served over HTTPS:

Production: https://observearth.com/api/
Local Dev:   http://localhost:8000/api/

items.title: Authentication Header
items.text:
Every request requires your API key passed in the X-API-Key HTTP header:

X-API-Key: 123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000
Content-Type: application/json

items.title: Standard HTTP Status Codes
items.text:
ObservEarth adheres strictly to RESTful conventions and standard HTTP status codes:

Code Status Meaning 200 OK Success Request succeeded. Response body contains requested resource or results. 201 Created Created Resource successfully created (e.g., Geometry, Alert). Location and details returned. 202 Accepted Processing Request accepted for asynchronous processing (e.g., Batch Data Request). 204 No Content Deleted Resource successfully deleted. No response body returned. 400 Bad Request Validation Error Missing parameters, invalid GeoJSON, bad date formats, or area limits exceeded. 401 Unauthorized Auth Missing No X-API-Key header provided or invalid key. 403 Forbidden Auth Invalid API key is inactive or lacks permission for the requested service. 404 Not Found Not Found Requested geometry_id, job_id, or alert_id does not exist. 429 Too Many Requests Rate Limited Exceeded per-minute or monthly call allowance. Includes Retry-After header. 500 Server Error Internal Error Unexpected server error. Contact office@rottengrapes.tech if persistent.

items.title: Universal Error Response Format
items.text:
When an API call returns a 4xx or 5xx error, the response payload contains a standardized JSON error message:

{
  "error": "Descriptive error message explaining what failed",
  "detail": "Optional auxiliary technical details or field validation breakdowns"
}

items.title: Geometry Identification Convention
items.text:
In ObservEarth, all satellite, weather, and terrain queries bind to a registered AOI identified by its geometry_id (a UUIDv4 string):

  • Path Parameter Style: /api/s2/image/{geometry_id}/
  • Query Parameter Style: /api/weather/current/?geometry_id={geometry_id}
  • JSON Body Parameter Style: {"geometry_id": "123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000", ...}

items.title: Supported Output Formats
items.text:
Depending on the endpoint, ObservEarth supports multiple response formats:

  • application/json: GeoJSON FeatureCollections, statistical summaries, search results, weather forecasts, and usage logs.
  • image/png: Rendered true-color RGB or colormapped vegetation index rasters with transparent backgrounds.
  • image/tiff / image/geotiff: Calibrated multi-band or single-band 32-bit floating-point Cloud-Optimized GeoTIFFs (COG) with embedded geospatial metadata (CRS, Affine transformation).

items.title: Sentinel-1 (SAR Radar) API
items.text: The Sentinel-1 API provides all-weather, day-and-night Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) imagery acquired by the Copernicus Sentinel-1 constellation (C-band radar, 5.405 GHz). It is used for soil moisture tracking, flood mapping, and crop canopy structure analysis.

items.title: Sentinel-2 (Optical) API
items.text: The Sentinel-2 API provides access to high-resolution (10m and 20m) multispectral imagery acquired by the Copernicus Sentinel-2 constellation (Sentinel-2A and Sentinel-2B). ObservEarth processes Sentinel-2 Level-2A Bottom-Of-Atmosphere (BOA) surface reflectance with automatic cloud masking and index computation.

items.title: cURL Command Cheatsheet
items.text: Quick reference of ready-to-run curl commands for all 56 ObservEarth endpoints. Replace YOUR_API_KEY, YOUR_GEOMETRY_ID, SCENE_ID, JOB_ID, and ALERT_ID with your actual values.

items.title: Authentication & Verification
items.text:
# Verify API Key status and quota
curl -X POST "https://observearth.com/api/verify-api-key/" \
     -H "X-API-Key: YOUR_API_KEY" \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -d '{"api_key": "YOUR_API_KEY"}'

items.title: Geometry / AOI Management
items.text:
# 1. List Geometries (Paginated)
curl -X GET "https://observearth.com/api/geometry/?page=1&page_size=20" \
     -H "X-API-Key: YOUR_API_KEY"

# 2. Register New Geometry / AOI
curl -X POST "https://observearth.com/api/geometry/" \
     -H "X-API-Key: YOUR_API_KEY" \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -d '{
       "name": "Central Valley Field 4",
       "geometry": {
         "type": "Polygon",
         "coordinates": [[
           [-120.45, 36.52], [-120.44, 36.52],
           [-120.44, 36.53], [-120.45, 36.53],
           [-120.45, 36.52]
         ]]
       },
       "lookback_months": 1
     }'

# 3. Get Geometry Details & GeoJSON Boundary
curl -X GET "https://observearth.com/api/geometry/YOUR_GEOMETRY_ID/" \
     -H "X-API-Key: YOUR_API_KEY"

# 4. Update Geometry Name / Daily Cron
curl -X PUT "https://observearth.com/api/geometry/YOUR_GEOMETRY_ID/" \
     -H "X-API-Key: YOUR_API_KEY" \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -d '{"name": "Central Valley Field 4 - North Sector", "daily_cron": true}'

# 5. Delete Geometry (Releases Allocated Hectares)
curl -X DELETE "https://observearth.com/api/geometry/YOUR_GEOMETRY_ID/" \
     -H "X-API-Key: YOUR_API_KEY"

items.title: Sentinel-2 (Optical Imagery & Indices)
items.text:
# 1. Search Filtered Sentinel-2 Scenes
curl -X POST "https://observearth.com/api/s2/search/" \
     -H "X-API-Key: YOUR_API_KEY" \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -d '{
       "geometry_id": "YOUR_GEOMETRY_ID",
       "start_date": "2026-05-01",
       "end_date": "2026-05-31",
       "cloud_cover": 20
     }'

# 2. Single Item Statistics (NDVI)
curl -X GET "https://observearth.com/api/s2/stats/YOUR_GEOMETRY_ID/?item_id=S2A_MSIL2A_20260517T183921_R070_T11SKB_20260517T221543&index=ndvi" \
     -H "X-API-Key: YOUR_API_KEY"

# 3. Multi-Scene Time-Series Statistics across Date Range
curl -X POST "https://observearth.com/api/s2/stats/" \
     -H "X-API-Key: YOUR_API_KEY" \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -d '{
       "geometry_id": "YOUR_GEOMETRY_ID",
       "start_date": "2026-05-01",
       "end_date": "2026-05-31",
       "index": "ndvi",
       "cloud_cover": 20
     }'

# 4. Render Colormapped Index Image (PNG)
curl -X POST "https://observearth.com/api/s2/image/YOUR_GEOMETRY_ID/" \
     -H "X-API-Key: YOUR_API_KEY" \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -d '{
       "item_id": "S2A_MSIL2A_20260517T183921_R070_T11SKB_20260517T221543",
       "index": "ndvi",
       "image_type": "png",
       "colormap": "rdylgn"
     }' --output s2_ndvi.png

# 5. All-in-One Multi-Index Bundle (8+ Indices Computed Together)
curl -X POST "https://observearth.com/api/s2/all-in-one/" \
     -H "X-API-Key: YOUR_API_KEY" \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -d '{
       "geometry_id": "YOUR_GEOMETRY_ID",
       "item_id": "S2A_MSIL2A_20260517T183921_R070_T11SKB_20260517T221543",
       "indices": ["ndvi", "ndwi", "evi", "savi", "ndre", "msavi", "vari"]
     }'

# 6. Fetch Raw Calibrated Spectral Band (NIR Band 8)
curl -X GET "https://observearth.com/api/s2/raw-band/YOUR_GEOMETRY_ID/?item_id=S2A_MSIL2A_20260517T183921_R070_T11SKB_20260517T221543&band=nir&image_type=tif" \
     -H "X-API-Key: YOUR_API_KEY" \
     --output s2_nir_band.tif

# 7. Submit Asynchronous Batch Extraction Job
curl -X POST "https://observearth.com/api/s2/data-request/" \
     -H "X-API-Key: YOUR_API_KEY" \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -d '{
       "geometry_id": "YOUR_GEOMETRY_ID",
       "start_date": "2026-05-01",
       "end_date": "2026-05-31",
       "index": "ndvi",
       "cloud_cover": 15,
       "format": "geotiff"
     }'

# 8. Poll Asynchronous Batch Job Status
curl -X GET "https://observearth.com/api/s2/data-request/status/JOB_ID/" \
     -H "X-API-Key: YOUR_API_KEY"

# 9. View Asynchronous Job Request History
curl -X GET "https://observearth.com/api/s2/data-request/history/" \
     -H "X-API-Key: YOUR_API_KEY"

# 10. List All 45+ Supported Sentinel-2 Indices
curl -X GET "https://observearth.com/api/s2/info/" \
     -H "X-API-Key: YOUR_API_KEY"

items.title: Automated Alerts & Notifications
items.text:
# 1. Create Automated Monitoring Rule
curl -X POST "https://observearth.com/api/alerts/" \
     -H "X-API-Key: YOUR_API_KEY" \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -d '{
       "geometry_id": "YOUR_GEOMETRY_ID",
       "name": "Vegetation Stress & Drought Watch",
       "logic": "AND",
       "monitor_until": "2026-11-30",
       "conditions": [
         {"index": "ndvi", "operator": "<", "threshold": 0.35},
         {"index": "ndwi", "operator": "<", "threshold": -0.10}
       ]
     }'

# 2. List All Active and Archived Alert Rules
curl -X GET "https://observearth.com/api/alerts/" \
     -H "X-API-Key: YOUR_API_KEY"

# 3. Get Alert Rule Details
curl -X GET "https://observearth.com/api/alerts/ALERT_ID/" \
     -H "X-API-Key: YOUR_API_KEY"

# 4. Update Alert Rule Parameters
curl -X PUT "https://observearth.com/api/alerts/ALERT_ID/" \
     -H "X-API-Key: YOUR_API_KEY" \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -d '{
       "name": "Vegetation Stress - Tightened",
       "logic": "AND",
       "monitor_until": "2026-12-31",
       "conditions": [{"index": "ndvi", "operator": "<", "threshold": 0.30}]
     }'

# 5. Toggle Alert Rule Active / Inactive State
curl -X PATCH "https://observearth.com/api/alerts/ALERT_ID/" \
     -H "X-API-Key: YOUR_API_KEY" \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -d '{"is_active": false}'

# 6. Delete Alert Rule
curl -X DELETE "https://observearth.com/api/alerts/ALERT_ID/" \
     -H "X-API-Key: YOUR_API_KEY"

# 7. List Triggered Alert Notifications

     -H "X-API-Key: YOUR_API_KEY"

# 8. Mark Triggered Notification as Read

items.text: Interact with ObservEarth using modern JavaScript (ES Modules, fetch, or Axios) in Node.js or backend environments.

items.title: Code Example (Node.js Fetch API)
items.text:
const BASE_URL = 'https://observearth.com/api';
const API_KEY = process.env.OBSERVEARTH_API_KEY || 'YOUR_API_KEY_HERE';

const headers = {
  'X-API-Key': API_KEY,
  'Content-Type': 'application/json'
};

// 1. Verify API Key
async function verifyKey() {
  const res = await fetch(`${BASE_URL}/verify-api-key/`, {
    method: 'POST',
    headers,
    body: JSON.stringify({ api_key: API_KEY })
  });
  const data = await res.json();
  console.log('API Key Valid:', data.valid);
}

// 2. Register Farm AOI
async function registerAOI() {
  const payload = {
    name: 'Sector 4 Orchard',
    geometry: {
      type: 'Polygon',
      coordinates: [[
        [-120.450, 36.520],
        [-120.440, 36.520],
        [-120.440, 36.530],
        [-120.450, 36.530],
        [-120.450, 36.520]
      ]]
    },
    lookback_months: 1
  };

  const res = await fetch(`${BASE_URL}/geometry/`, {
    method: 'POST',
    headers,
    body: JSON.stringify(payload)
  });

  if (res.status === 201) {
    const data = await res.json();
    console.log(`AOI Created: ${data.id} (${data.properties.area} ha)`);
    return data.id;
  } else {
    const err = await res.json();
    console.error('Error:', err);
    return null;
  }
}

// 3. Get Current Weather & Soil Telemetry
async function fetchWeather(geometryId) {
  const res = await fetch(`${BASE_URL}/weather/current/?geometry_id=${geometryId}`, {
    headers
  });
  const data = await res.json();
  console.log('Current Weather:', data.current);
}

async function main() {
  await verifyKey();
  const geometryId = await registerAOI();
  if (geometryId) {
    await fetchWeather(geometryId);
  }
}

main().catch(console.error);

items.title: Python Integration Guide
items.text: A complete, production-ready Python example demonstrating how to interact with ObservEarth: creating a farm geometry, discovering Sentinel-2 imagery, computing NDVI statistics, and retrieving current weather.

items.title: Installation
items.text: pip install requests python-dotenv

items.title: Complete Integration Script
items.text:
import os
import requests
import json

BASE_URL = "https://observearth.com/api"
API_KEY = os.getenv("OBSERVEARTH_API_KEY", "YOUR_API_KEY_HERE")

headers = {
    "X-API-Key": API_KEY,
    "Content-Type": "application/json"
}

def verify_key():
    url = f"{BASE_URL}/verify-api-key/"
    res = requests.post(url, headers=headers, json={"api_key": API_KEY})
    print("API Key Verification:", res.json())

def create_farm_aoi():
    url = f"{BASE_URL}/geometry/"
    payload = {
        "name": "Demo Vineyard",
        "geometry": {
            "type": "Polygon",
            "coordinates": [
                [
                    [-120.450, 36.520],
                    [-120.440, 36.520],
                    [-120.440, 36.530],
                    [-120.450, 36.530],
                    [-120.450, 36.520]
                ]
            ]
        },
        "lookback_months": 1
    }
    res = requests.post(url, headers=headers, json=payload)
    if res.status_code == 201:
        data = res.json()
        print(f"Created AOI ID: {data['id']} (Area: {data['properties']['area']} ha)")
        return data["id"]
    else:
        print("Error creating geometry:", res.status_code, res.text)
        return None

def search_satellite_imagery(geometry_id):
    url = f"{BASE_URL}/s2/search/"
    payload = {
        "geometry_id": geometry_id,
        "start_date": "2026-05-01",
        "end_date": "2026-05-31",
        "cloud_cover": 20
    }
    res = requests.post(url, headers=headers, json=payload)
    results = res.json().get("results", [])
    print(f"Found {len(results)} clean Sentinel-2 passes.")
    return results

def get_ndvi_statistics(geometry_id, item_id):
    url = f"{BASE_URL}/s2/stats/{geometry_id}/"
    params = {
        "item_id": item_id,
        "index": "ndvi"
    }
    res = requests.get(url, headers=headers, params=params)
    print("NDVI Stats:", json.dumps(res.json(), indent=2))

def get_current_weather(geometry_id):
    url = f"{BASE_URL}/weather/current/"
    params = {"geometry_id": geometry_id}
    res = requests.get(url, headers=headers, params=params)
    weather = res.json().get("current", {})
    print(f"Temperature: {weather.get('temp')}°C | Humidity: {weather.get('relative_humidity')}% | Soil Temp (Surface): {weather.get('soil_temperature_surface')}°C")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    verify_key()
    geom_id = create_farm_aoi()
    if geom_id:
        scenes = search_satellite_imagery(geom_id)
        if scenes:
            best_scene = scenes[0]["id"]
            get_ndvi_statistics(geom_id, best_scene)
        get_current_weather(geom_id)

items.title: Creating an Account
items.text: Getting started with ObservEarth takes less than two minutes. This guide walks you through registering an account, understanding initial quotas, logging in, and managing your profile.

items.title: 1. Navigate to the Signup Page
items.text: Visit the ObservEarth registration portal at https://observearth.com/signup/ (or /signup/ on your local deployment).

items.title: 2. Complete the Signup Form
items.text:
Provide your account credentials:

  • Username: A unique alphanumeric handle used for dashboard sign-in and identification.
  • Email Address: Used for critical system notifications, billing updates, and alert triggers.
  • Password: Must be at least 8 characters long and follow secure password guidelines.
  • Confirm Password: Re-enter password for verification.

items.title: 3. Immediate Activation
items.text:
Upon clicking Create Account, your account is provisioned instantly:

  • User record created: Your account credentials become active immediately.
  • API Key assigned: A unique UUIDv4 API key is automatically generated.
  • Initial land quota: You receive default access to 500 hectares (5,000,000 m² / 5 sq km) of cumulative area coverage on the Research & Non-commercial plan.
  • Sensors unlocked: Full access is granted to Sentinel-2, Sentinel-1, Landsat, MODIS, and weather services.
  • Workspace ready: You are redirected to your active Dashboard.

items.title: Logging In
items.text:
If you already have an account:

  1. Navigate to https://observearth.com/login/ (or /login/).
  2. Input your registered Username and Password.
  3. Click Log In.
  4. You will land directly on /dashboard/.

items.title: Profile & Password Management
items.text:
You can update your personal information or rotate your web dashboard credentials at any time from /dashboard/profile/:

  • Personal details: Update your first name, last name, and display name.
  • Email address: Keep your email current to ensure timely delivery of satellite alert notifications.
  • Subscription tier: View your current plan (Paid or Research) and upgrade your quota.
  • Password updates: Supply your current password and set a new password to maintain account security.

items.title: Next Steps
items.text: Now that your account is created, proceed to API Keys & Authentication to retrieve your key and make your first authenticated request.

items.title: API Keys & Authentication
items.text: Every API call made to the ObservEarth REST API requires programmatic authentication via a unique API Key.

items.title: How to Get Your API Key
items.text:
Your API key is generated automatically when your account is registered. To locate and copy your key:

  1. Log into your ObservEarth account at https://observearth.com/login/.
  2. In the left navigation menu, click API Usage (or visit /dashboard/api-usage/).
  3. You will see your API Key presented in a secure card.
  4. Click the Reveal eye icon to view the key, or click Copy to copy the string directly to your clipboard.

[!WARNING] Your API key grants programmatic access to your registered areas, data processing jobs, and account allowances. Treat it like a secret password. Never commit your API key to public source code repositories (like GitHub or GitLab), client-side JavaScript applications, or mobile binaries.

items.title: Passing the API Key in Requests
items.text:
ObservEarth uses standard HTTP header-based authentication. Pass your API key in the X-API-Key HTTP header:

X-API-Key: 123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000

items.title: Supported Header Names:
items.text:
• X-API-Key (Recommended standard)
  • x-api-key (Lowercase HTTP/2 standard)

items.title: Verifying an API Key
items.text: You can test whether an API key is valid and active using the dedicated verification endpoint. This endpoint does not count against your billable rate limits.

items.title: Endpoint
items.text: POST /api/verify-api-key/

items.title: Request Headers
items.text: Header Type Required Description X-API-Key String (UUID) No* The API key to test (*or pass in request body) Content-Type String Yes application/json

items.title: cURL Request
items.text:
curl -X POST "https://observearth.com/api/verify-api-key/" \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -d '{"api_key": "123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000"}'

items.title: Response (200 OK)
items.text:
{
  "valid": true
}

If the key does not exist or has been disabled: 

{
  "valid": false
}

items.title: Authentication Status Codes & Error Handling
items.text:
When making API calls, ObservEarth returns standard HTTP response codes for authentication issues:

Status Code Reason Cause Solution 401 Unauthorized Missing API Key No X-API-Key header provided Add -H "X-API-Key: <key>" to your request 403 Forbidden Invalid API Key The provided UUID is invalid, unrecognised, or deactivated Verify key in /dashboard/api-usage/ 429 Too Many Requests Rate Limit Exceeded Per-minute or monthly threshold crossed Implement exponential backoff or upgrade plan

items.title: Standard 401 Error Response
items.text:
{
  "error": "Authentication credentials were not provided."
}

items.title: Standard 403 Error Response
items.text:
{
  "error": "Invalid or inactive API key provided."
}

items.title: 1. Store API Keys in Environment Variables
items.text:
Never hardcode your API key inside your source files. Use .env files and environment variable loaders:

  • Separation of secrets: Keep sensitive tokens separate from version-controlled source code.
  • Easy rotation: Update environment variables without needing code redeployment.
import os
import requests

OBSERVEARTH_API_KEY = os.getenv("OBSERVEARTH_API_KEY")

headers = {
    "X-API-Key": OBSERVEARTH_API_KEY,
    "Content-Type": "application/json"
}
response = requests.get("https://observearth.com/api/geometry/", headers=headers)

items.title: 2. Use a Backend Proxy for Web and Mobile Apps
items.text:
If you are developing a customer-facing frontend (such as React, Vue, Flutter, iOS, or Android):

  • Route requests through your server: Make API calls from your backend server, which attaches the secret API key.
  • Prevent key leakage: Do not expose X-API-Key in browser network tabs or mobile app binaries.

items.title: Plans, Quotas & Limits
items.text: ObservEarth operates on an Area of Interest (AOI) footprint model combined with fair-use request rate limits to guarantee high availability and sub-second raster tile streaming.

items.title: Subscription Plans & Area Allowances
items.text:
When you define farm boundaries or geographic monitoring areas (AOIs), ObservEarth calculates the real-world surface area in hectares using UTM coordinate transformations. Your account plan determines the total cumulative area you can have active concurrently.

Plan Tier Display Name Max Cumulative Area Single Farm Size Limit Target Audience Free Research & Non-commercial 500 Hectares (5 km²) Up to 100 Hectares Students, independent researchers, pilots Startup Startup & Non-Profit 5,000 Hectares (50 km²) Up to 500 Hectares Agritech startups, field trials, cooperatives Giant Giant Enterprise 30,000 Hectares (300 km²) Up to 2,000 Hectares Forestry firms, regional irrigation boards Super Giant Super Giant Enterprise 100,000+ Hectares (1,000+ km²) Custom National monitoring, multinational insurers

[!NOTE] The cumulative area limit applies to active geometries. If you delete an inactive geometry using DELETE /api/geometry/<id>/, that area is immediately released back to your available budget!

items.title: Single Farm Size Enforcement
items.text:
To prevent raster generation latency spikes on oversized polygons, individual geometries have maximum allowable single-farm size checks:

  • Free tier limit: Single geometries cannot exceed 100 hectares.
  • Startup tier limit: Single geometries cannot exceed 500 hectares.
  • Error handling: If a polygon exceeds the limit, the API returns 400 Bad Request:
{
  "error": "Single farm size cannot exceed 100.00 hectares. This farm is 142.50 hectares."
}

items.title: API Request Rate Limits
items.text:
Every plan includes generous rate limits broken down by functional API Types:

API Type Scope & Endpoints Included Per-Minute Limit Monthly Limit API Type 1 Satellite Catalog Search (/api/s2/search/, /api/s1/search/, /api/landsat/search/, /api/modis/search/) 300 req / min 50,000 req / month API Type 2 Satellite Raster Data, Imagery & Stats (/api/*/image/, /api/*/stats/, /api/*/raw-band/, /api/s2/sen2sr/*) 300 req / min 50,000 req / month API Type 3 Weather Data (/api/weather/current/, /api/weather/today/, /api/weather/forecast/, /api/weather/historical/) 100 req / min 20,000 req / month API Type 4 Air Quality Data (/api/air-quality/current/, /api/air-quality/today/, /api/air-quality/forecast/, /api/air-quality/historical/) 100 req / min 5,000 req / month

items.title: Checking Your Current Usage
items.text: You can inspect your real-time cumulative area usage, percentage of plan utilized, and monthly call counts via both the web UI and programmatic APIs:

items.title: 1. Web Dashboard
items.text:
Navigate to /dashboard/ or /dashboard/api-usage/ to see visual progress bars showing:

  • Active farm count: Number of monitored geometries currently saved in your account.
  • Hectares consumed: Real-world footprint currently active versus your plan's maximum allowance.
  • Usage percentage: Percentage of total area utilized with colored progress indicator.

items.title: 2. Programmatic API
items.text: Call GET /api/analytics/summary/current/ (detailed in the API Analytics Guide) to receive a machine-readable breakdown of your current month's calls across every satellite and weather service.

items.title: Area of Interest (AOI) Management
items.text: In ObservEarth, an Area of Interest (AOI) or Geometry represents the physical boundary of an agricultural field, forest parcel, urban zone, or water reservoir. Every satellite calculation, weather extraction, and alert rule operates against a registered AOI.

items.title: Defining an AOI
items.text: An AOI is defined as a GeoJSON Polygon or MultiPolygon in the standard WGS84 (EPSG:4326) coordinate reference system (longitude, latitude coordinates).

items.title: GeoJSON Structure
items.text:
{
  "type": "Polygon",
  "coordinates": [
    [
      [77.5854, 12.9682],
      [77.5954, 12.9682],
      [77.5954, 12.9782],
      [77.5854, 12.9782],
      [77.5854, 12.9682]
    ]
  ]
}

[!IMPORTANT] The coordinate array must form a closed linear ring: the first and last coordinate pair must be identical!

items.title: Creating an AOI via Web Dashboard
items.text:
To define a boundary using the visual interface:

  1. Navigate to Add AOI (/dashboard/add-aoi/) in the dashboard menu.
  2. Enter a descriptive Farm Name (e.g., North Sector Corn Field).
  3. Use the interactive drawing toolbar on the top-right of the map to trace your field boundary:
  4. Click each vertex around your parcel.
  5. Double-click to close the polygon.
  6. Alternatively, drag and drop a .geojson, .kml, or zipped .shp file.
  7. The system calculates the area in real-time.
  8. Click Save AOI.

items.title: Automated Background Ingestion
items.text:
When a new AOI is created (either through the dashboard or via POST /api/geometry/):

  1. Polygon Normalization: The boundary is checked for self-intersections and normalized.
  2. UTM Projection & Area Computation: The polygon is transformed to the local Universal Transverse Mercator (UTM) zone for millimeter-precise area calculation in hectares.
  3. Historical Data Ingestion: A background Celery worker initiates historical satellite ingestion across the specified lookback window (default: 1 month, up to 12+ months).
  4. Automated Daily Monitoring: The daily_cron flag (enabled by default) ensures the field is scanned automatically every morning for newly available satellite scenes.

items.title: Managing Existing AOIs
items.text:
From the dashboard table (/dashboard/):

  • View Details: Opens the satellite explorer at /dashboard/aoi/<geometry_id>/.
  • Weather Station: Opens the microclimate and soil moisture monitor at /dashboard/aoi/<geometry_id>/weather/.
  • Edit: Rename the parcel or toggle daily_cron automated daily processing.
  • Delete: Remove the geometry. Deleting immediately releases the parcel's hectarage back to your account's area quota.

items.title: Platform Walkthrough: Automated Alerts & Monitoring
items.text:
Access Notifications (/dashboard/alerts/ or /notifications/) to set up automated threshold alerts across your fields on ObservEarth.

Whenever a newly ingested satellite pass occurs, ObservEarth automatically evaluates your conditions and sends out notifications.

items.title: 1. Alert Rule Management
items.text:
• Add Alert Button: Click the green + Add Alert button to configure a new monitoring rule for any of your registered AOIs.
  • Tabs Navigation:
  • Notification History: Audit feed of all past triggered alerts with timestamps, recorded values, and farm associations.
  • Alerts: Current active monitoring rules configured for your account.

items.title: 2. Rule Configuration & Fields
items.text:
• Farm: Select the target monitored parcel (e.g., Demo 2, Field 4).
  • Alert Name: Custom label assigned to the rule (e.g., Vegetation Stress & Drought Watch).
  • Logic: Boolean combination logic (AND / OR).
  • Conditions: Multi-condition expressions (e.g., NDVI < 0.35, NDWI < -0.10).
  • Monitor Until: Rule expiration date (e.g., Nov. 30, 2026).
  • Status: Active status badge (Active or Paused).
  • Actions:
  • Toggle Switch: Instant enable or pause of active monitoring.
  • Delete (Red Trash Icon): Permanently delete rule.

items.title: Platform Walkthrough: AOI Creation & Drawing
items.text:
Registering an Area of Interest (AOI) is the first step toward extracting satellite analytics, high-resolution imagery, and weather telemetry on ObservEarth.

Navigate to Add AOI (/dashboard/add-aoi/) or click the green + Add New AOI button from the dashboard.

items.title: Step 1: Configure AOI Properties
items.text:
• AOI Name: Enter an identifiable name for your field or project (e.g., Central Valley Field 4).
  • Look Back Months: Specify the historical satellite archive depth to scan upon registration (default: 1 month). ObservEarth automatically indexes all cloud-filtered scenes acquired within this period.
  • Selection Method:
  • Draw on Map: Trace parcel boundaries manually on the interactive Leaflet map.
  • Upload GeoJSON/Shapefile: Upload .geojson, .kml, or zipped .shp files for instant boundary parsing.

items.title: Step 2: Trace Boundary on Interactive Map
items.text:
• Use the top search bar to locate your town, region, or latitude/longitude coordinates.
  • Click anywhere on the map canvas to place perimeter vertex nodes.
  • Double-click on the starting vertex or press enter to close the polygon ring.
  • Drag existing vertex markers to fine-tune boundaries to fence lines or natural parcel borders.

items.title: Step 3: Real-Time Footprint Telemetry
items.text:
The telemetry bar at the bottom updates live as you place nodes:

  • Live Area Calculation: Computes geodesic surface area dynamically in hectares (ha) and square meters (m²).
  • Perimeter Calculation: Calculates perimeter distance in kilometers (km).
  • Clear: Reset the current canvas and start a new boundary drawing.

items.title: Step 4: Save & Background Ingestion
items.text:
• Click the green Create AOI button.
  • ObservEarth's backend Celery worker normalizes the polygon into WGS 84 (EPSG:4326), validates against your plan's maximum single AOI limit, checks available monthly hectare quota, and triggers historical scene cataloging across Sentinel-2, Sentinel-1, Landsat, and MODIS.

items.title: Platform Walkthrough: API Usage & Key Analytics
items.text: Navigate to API Usage (/dashboard/api-usage/) to inspect your production credentials, track consumption against your quota, and analyze request performance on ObservEarth.

items.title: Key Management & Quota Tracking
items.text:
• Your API Access Key: Secure card displaying your masked secret key. Click the yellow eye icon to reveal the key, or click the copy icon to copy it to your clipboard.
  • Authentication Header: Pass this key in the X-API-Key HTTP header for all programmatic API requests.
  • Area Processed Progress Bar: Real-time progress bar displaying cumulative unique hectares processed (e.g., 2199.14 / 5000.00 Hectares).
  • Time Range Filters: Select telemetry intervals across 24h, 7d, 15d, or Custom.
  • Real-Time KPIs:
  • Total Requests: Cumulative calls executed (e.g., 10).
  • Average Latency: Response execution speed (e.g., 2980 ms).
  • Satellite Queries: Total queries directed to satellite pipelines (e.g., 6).
  • Weather & AQ Queries: Total queries directed to weather and air quality endpoints (e.g., 4).
  • API Category Summary Count: Live counters broken down by Search, Stats, All-in-One, Images, Weather, and Air Quality APIs.

items.title: 2. Request Volume Charts & Category Breakdowns
items.text: Scroll down on the API Usage page to inspect visual performance and endpoint distribution graphs.

items.title: Performance Visualizations
items.text:
• Request Timeline (Last 7 Days): Line chart tracking daily API request volume trends.
  • Satellite Usage Donut Chart: Breakdown of queries across Sentinel-2, Sentinel-1, Landsat, and MODIS constellations.
  • API Category Breakdown Bar Chart: Visual comparison across Search, Stats, Images, Weather, and Air Quality endpoints.
  • Weather & AQ Endpoints Pie Chart: Distribution of queries across Current, Today, Forecast, and Historical datasets.

items.title: 3. Historical Usage Audits (Past Months Summary)
items.text: Click the Past Stats button in the top right of the API Usage dashboard to audit historical billing periods.

items.title: Historical Audit Features
items.text:
• Year & Month Selector: Select past calendar years and months (e.g., October 2026) and click Fetch Summary.
  • Archived Category Breakdown: Displays historical call counts across Search APIs, Stats APIs, Images APIs, Weather APIs, Air Quality, and overall satellite sensor distribution.
  • Latency & Execution Records: Review historical average execution latency for compliance and capacity planning.

items.title: Platform Walkthrough: Constellations & Index Directory
items.text: Explore the multi-sensor Earth Observation catalog, search over 45 supported spectral formulas, and access developer playgrounds on ObservEarth.

items.title: 1. Supported Satellite Constellations
items.text: Navigate to Satellites (/satellites/) from the top navigation bar to explore supported satellite constellations.

items.title: Constellation Capabilities
items.text:
• Landsat 8 & 9: USGS / NASA optical and thermal bands at 30m resolution with specialized vegetation and thermal indices.
  • Sentinel-1: ESA C-band Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) with all-weather surface roughness and moisture penetrating capabilities (5m to 40m resolution).
  • Sentinel-2: ESA multispectral imagery at 10m to 60m resolution supporting 22+ vegetation, water, soil, and fire indices.
  • MODIS: Terra & Aqua daily 250m/500m composites for regional timeseries.

items.title: 2. Sentinel-2 Spectral Indices Directory
items.text: Clicking View indices under Sentinel-2 opens the dedicated index catalog (/satellites/sentinel-2/).

items.title: Index Catalog Features
items.text:
• Instant Search Bar: Filter indices dynamically by keyword or acronym (e.g., ARVI, BSI, CCCI, EVI, NDVI).
  • Category Filters: Filter by application: All, Vegetation, Soil, Fire, Water, Custom, Urban, Snow.
  • Interactive Index Cards:
  • ARVI (Atmospherically Resistant Vegetation Index): Uses blue, red, and NIR bands with RdYlGn colormap (scale: 0.0 to 1.0).
  • BSI (Bare Soil Index): Uses SWIR16, red, NIR, and blue bands with YlOrBr colormap (scale: -1.0 to 1.0).
  • CCCI (Canopy Chlorophyll Content Index): Uses NIR, red edge, and red bands with YlGn colormap (scale: 0.0 to 5.0).
  • Click View Details on any card to view exact mathematical formulas, band wavelengths, and citation papers.

items.title: 3. Interactive Developer API Hub (Swagger & ReDoc)
items.text: Navigate to API Docs (/api/) to access interactive API playgrounds and download offline reference materials.

items.title: Developer Documentation Tools
items.text:
• Interactive Swagger UI: Test REST API endpoints live in your browser with parameter validation and instant JSON response formatting.
  • ReDoc Interface: Clean, responsive, 3-panel documentation view ideal for integration engineers.
  • Spectral Indices Reference PDF: Download an offline manual of all spectral formulas, SAR polarizations, MODIS collections, and default colormap stretch boundaries.

items.title: Platform Walkthrough: Dashboard Overview
items.text: The Main Dashboard (/dashboard/) serves as your operational command center on ObservEarth. It provides a real-time summary of your monitored land footprint, quota consumption, and saved farm boundaries.

items.title: 1. Top Telemetry Cards
items.text:
• Total AOIs: Real-time counter of all registered parcels (e.g., 148 active fields).
  • Total Area: Cumulative geographic land area monitored by ObservEarth (e.g., 2199.14 hectares).
  • Area Usage Gauge: Real-time capacity progress bar showing consumed hectares against your monthly subscription tier allowance (e.g., 44.0% utilized of 5000.00 hectares).

items.title: 2. Monitored Areas of Interest (AOI) Inventory
items.text:
The AOI table lists every parcel saved under your account:

  • Search AOIs: Type any farm name or coordinate keyword into the search bar to filter records instantly.
  • Page Size Selector: Switch between 10, 20, 50, or 100 records per view.
  • Field Name & Calculated Area: Displays each parcel's custom label and geodesic surface area in hectares (e.g., 15.41 ha, 4.05 ha, 28.57 ha).

items.title: 3. Quick Action Controls
items.text:
Each row in the inventory table provides one-click operational shortcuts:

  • View Details (Blue Eye Icon): Opens the Satellite Explorer & Analytics page (/dashboard/aoi/<id>/) to inspect spectral indices, cloud cover filters, and date ribbons.
  • Weather (Blue Sun Icon): Opens the dedicated Agrometeorological Weather Station (/dashboard/aoi/<id>/weather/) for live sensor telemetry and 7-day agronomic forecasts.
  • Notifications (Yellow Bell Icon): Opens the field's Automated Threshold Alerts monitoring rules.
  • Edit (Pencil Icon): Update the parcel boundary, name, or metadata.
  • Delete (Red Trash Icon): Permanently deletes the field and immediately releases hectares back to your account quota.

items.title: Platform Walkthrough: Satellite Explorer & Analytics
items.text: Clicking View Details (blue eye icon) on any farm in the dashboard opens the AOI Explorer (/dashboard/aoi/<id>/). Here you can search multi-constellation imagery, select from 45+ spectral indices, render colormapped rasters, and inspect zonal statistics.

items.title: Control Toolbar Capabilities
items.text:
• Satellite Selector: Switch between constellations:
  • Sentinel 2: 10m to 20m optical multispectral imagery with 5-day revisit cycles.
  • Sentinel 1: 10m C-band Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) for all-weather moisture and flood penetration.
  • Landsat: 30m optical and thermal infrared multispectral data.
  • MODIS: Daily global coverage across 250m and 500m land bands.
  • Index Category & Specific Formula: Filter by application category (All, Vegetation, Water, Soil, Urban, Fire, Stress, Snow) and pick from over 45 formulas (e.g., NDVI, EVI, NDRE, NDWI, BSI).
  • Cloud Cover Tolerance: Drag the slider (0% to 100%) to filter out cloud-obscured scenes (e.g., set to <= 30%).
  • Date Range Pickers: Define your observation window with Start Date and End Date.
  • Colormap & Value Stretch:
  • Choose your visualization palette (e.g., rdylgn — Red to Yellow to Green, viridis, plasma).
  • Set manual stretch bounds (e.g., min -1, max 1).
  • Toggle Pixelized to inspect raw sensor pixels without bilinear smoothing.
  • Search Images (Green button): Executes the catalog search.
  • Download Stats (CSV button): Exports statistical timeseries across all available passes.

items.title: Available Dates Carousel
items.text:
Populates with all discovered acquisitions (e.g., 112 dates found):

  • Displays acquisition date (e.g., 2026-11-14), satellite badge (SENTINEL2), and cloud cover percentage (e.g., 8.38%, 27.42%, 0.00%).
  • Action buttons allow one-click map projection, raster downloading, and statistics inspection.

items.title: 2. Interactive Map Rasters & Zonal Statistics
items.text: Selecting an acquisition date renders the processed satellite raster clipped precisely to your parcel boundaries and computes detailed zonal statistics.

items.title: Zonal Statistics Telemetry
items.text:
• Scene Cloud Cover: Percentage of cloud cover detected across the parent scene tile (e.g., 27.42%).
  • Mean & Median: Field-wide average (e.g., 0.334274) and median (e.g., 0.304079) vegetative vigor.
  • Min & Max: Lowest observed value (e.g., 0.093606) and peak canopy value (e.g., 0.838337).
  • Standard Deviation (Std): Spatial uniformity across the field (e.g., 0.132782).
  • Sum: Aggregate sum of all valid pixels within the boundary (e.g., 548.88).
  • Percentiles (2% & 98%): Outlier boundary thresholds (e.g., P2% 0.138278, P98% 0.653996).
  • Valid & Masked Pixels: Pixel breakdown (e.g., 1,642 valid pixels, 1,466 masked/exterior pixels, 52.83% valid coverage).
  • Get Image with Actual Min/Max: Re-renders the visualization stretched dynamically between the field's actual minimum and maximum observed values for maximum visual contrast.

items.title: Platform Walkthrough: Signup, Login & Profile
items.text: Welcome to the ObservEarth onboarding guide. This section covers account registration, user authentication, profile preferences, and subscription tier settings on observearth.com.

items.title: 1. Homepage & Landing Portal
items.text: The ObservEarth homepage provides an interactive introduction to the platform's multi-spectral remote sensing engine.

items.title: Key Portal Capabilities
items.text:
• Interactive Split-Screen Slider: Inspect before-and-after comparisons showing raw aerial imagery overlaid with false-color NDVI vegetation vigor heatmaps.
  • Industry Solutions: Pre-configured workflows for precision agriculture, forestry carbon tracking, urban heat island mapping, and mining operations.
  • Top Navigation Bar: One-click shortcuts to Features, Analytics, Comparison, About, Contact, Satellites, API Docs, and Pricing.
  • Quick Access: Click Get Started to create an account or click Login to enter your workspace.

items.title: 2. Creating an Account (Sign Up)
items.text: New users can register for an account in seconds at /signup/.

items.title: Registration Form Fields
items.text:
• Email Address: Used for billing confirmations, system alerts, and automated satellite notifications.
  • Username: A unique alphanumeric handle (up to 150 characters; letters, digits, and @/./+/-/_ permitted).
  • Password: Must be at least 8 characters long, cannot be entirely numeric, cannot be a commonly used password, and cannot match personal details.
  • Confirm Password: Re-enter the exact password to confirm.
  • Automatic Research Allocation: Every new account automatically receives an initial allowance of 500 hectares (5 km²) on the Research & Non-commercial plan.
  • Submit: Click the green Sign Up button to immediately activate your account and generate your private API key.

items.title: 3. Account Authentication (Log In)
items.text: Existing users can access their workspace at /login/.

items.title: Login Flow
items.text:
• Username & Password: Input your registered account credentials.
  • Remember Me: Check this box to keep your browser session active.
  • Log In: Click the green Log In button. Upon authentication, you are routed directly to your active Dashboard (/dashboard/).
  • Self-Service Links: Access the Sign Up link if you need a new account or Forgot your password? for automated credential recovery.

items.title: 4. Profile & Account Settings
items.text: Manage your personal details, credentials, and subscription status at /dashboard/profile/.

items.title: Profile Management Sections
items.text:
• Personal Information:
  • First Name & Last Name: Manage your account display identity.
  • Email Address: Update your registered email address.
  • Click Save Changes to persist your profile updates.
  • Subscription Status:
  • Displays your active plan tier (e.g. Paid or Research).
  • Click Upgrade Plan to increase your cumulative monitored area allowance or unlock higher API request rate limits.
  • Change Password:
  • Enter your Current Password and specify a New Password (minimum 8 characters) to maintain security.

items.title: Platform Walkthrough: Weather Station & Telemetry
items.text: Clicking the Weather (blue sun icon) from the dashboard or navigating to /dashboard/aoi/<id>/weather/ opens the live agrometeorological and soil telemetry station on ObservEarth.

items.title: Real-Time Weather Readings
items.text:
• Current Conditions Hero Card: Real-time ambient temperature (e.g., 28.6°C), sky condition (Sunny), timestamp, and "Feels like" index (27.5°C).
  • Relative Humidity: Real-time atmospheric moisture content (e.g., 24% with visual status bar).
  • Wind Velocity & Direction: Real-time wind speed and compass orientation (e.g., 11.2 km/h NE Direction), vital for spray drift avoidance.
  • Surface Pressure: Atmospheric barometric pressure reading (e.g., 945.6 hPa).
  • UV Index: Solar ultraviolet radiation intensity (e.g., 6.95 High).
  • Precipitation & Rain: Cumulative rainfall recorded over the past 24 hours (e.g., 0 mm).
  • Cloud Cover: Sky obscuration percentage (e.g., 25%).
  • Reference Evapotranspiration (ET0): Calculated crop water loss via the FAO-56 Penman-Monteith equation (e.g., 2.5 mm), providing data for irrigation scheduling.

items.title: 2. 7-Day Forecast & Historical Climate Trends
items.text: Scroll down on the Weather Station page to review daily agronomic projections and multi-week climate progressions.

items.title: Short-Term & Historical Forecast Tools
items.text:
• 7-Day Agronomic Forecast:
  • Daily forecast cards (Today through Friday) displaying weather icons, daily high and low temperatures (e.g., 30°C / 16°C), expected wind speed, and humidity.
  • Precipitation indicators highlight upcoming rain events (e.g., 3.0 mm rain on Friday).
  • Weather History Timeframe: Switch views across 1 Week (1W), 1 Month (1M), or 3 Months (3M).
  • Parameter Tabs: Switch historical trend curves between:
  • Temperature (°C)
  • Precipitation (mm)
  • Humidity (%)
  • Wind Speed (km/h)
  • Soil Temperature (°C)
  • Soil Moisture (m³/m³)
  • Interactive Area Chart: Illustrates diurnal fluctuations, temperature spikes, and moisture progressions over the selected period.
